digest.headline: Today's World Briefing: Why the Nvidia Rally Fizzled
digest.dek: What 7 major outlets covered for Wednesday, November 25, ranked by how widely each story was reported.
digest.overview: 190 distinct stories ran across 7 major outlets in the latest news cycle. The most widely covered was “Why the Nvidia Rally Fizzled”, reported by 6 outlets (BBC, CNBC, CNN, NBC News, NYT, WSJ). It was followed by “Army set to detonate a cache of lead explosives, sending toxic plume across Iowa” and “The Morning Risk Report: China’s Huawei Convicted of Fraud in U.S. Criminal Trial”. World Affairs dominated the agenda, accounting for 2 of the top 8 stories. Words that kept coming up: huang, jensen, nvidia, therapy, iowa, army.

paragraphs.title: Why the Nvidia Rally Fizzled
paragraphs.text: In technology, NBC News reports: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around. Nvidia’s decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang after pressure from Trump is intensifying bipartisan scrutiny of tech companies' ties to the administration. The Nvidia co-founder thanked the Trump administration while addressing staff the day after he was reinstated as CEO.

paragraphs.title: Army set to detonate a cache of lead explosives, sending toxic plume across Iowa
paragraphs.text: Around the world, NBC News reports: The Army plans to detonate a stockpile of unstable lead azide explosives in Iowa on Wednesday morning. Residents of Middletown, which adjoins an Army facility where dangerous chemicals will be detonated Wednesday, are taping up their doors and getting ready to flee. The Army is set to detonate an estimated 9,700 pounds of lead azide in Iowa.

paragraphs.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia lands in Spain a ‘free man’ after deportation battle
paragraphs.text: Meanwhile, NBC News reports: Kilmar Abrego Garcia has landed in Spain after leaving the United States at the end of a closely watched and controversial deportation battle that became a symbol for the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown. Kilmar Armando Abrego Garcia, who was wrongfully deported from the United States last year, arrived in Madrid on Wednesday, ending a 20-month legal fight.
